LESSON: READING 3.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.2: Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension, part of Strand 3 in Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why do we read? 2. How can we read faster?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read a variety of print and non-print texts of about 300 words,

2. identify events in a story or a passage of about 300 words with logical and fluent flow,

3. answer factual and inferential questions from a text of about 300 words,

4. work together to infer the meaning of vocabulary from contexts,

5. skim through a digital text of about 300 words focusing mainly on the title and illustrations,

6. scan for information such as vocabulary words and answer questions from print or digital text,

7. skim or scan a comic, magazine, newspaper or age-appropriate reader,

8. discuss and role-play events in texts based on the theme. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read a variety of print and non-print texts of about 300 words,
2. identify events in a story or a passage of about 300 words with logical and fluent flow,
3. answer factual and inferential questions from a text of about 300 words,
4. work together to infer the meaning of vocabulary from contexts,
5. skim through a digital text of about 300 words focusing mainly on the title and illustrations,
6. scan for information such as vocabulary words and answer questions from print or digital text,
7. skim or scan a comic, magazine, newspaper or age-appropriate reader,
8. discuss and role-play events in texts based on the theme. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and problem solving: This is developed as the learner uses logical thinking to answer factual and

inferential questions from a text of about 300 words.

• Digital Literacy: It is promoted as the learner is able to interact with digital devices to skim through digital texts focusing

on the title and illustrations.

Values:
● Social Justice: This is promoted as the learner accords peers equal opportunities to infer the meaning of vocabulary from

contexts.

● Respect: This is developed as the learner is able to demonstrate etiquette when dealing with peers in class during

common tasks.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship: This is fostered as the learner works with peers peacefully during group activities.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to connect the concept of etiquette and politeness to their daily interactions and in all other learning areas.
